approved_premise.title: The Angle That Wouldn't Match
approved_premise.logline: A routine beacon calibration turns into Deniz's first real test of whether patient observation can outweigh a mentor's doubt.
approved_premise.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor conducting supervised but semi-independent beacon calibration checks.
approved_premise.immediate_objective: Confirm whether a magnetic-stone beacon reading at Beacon Ridge is a genuine anomaly or an instrument error before the calibration window closes.
approved_premise.inciting_event: While logging a routine reading, Deniz notices the beacon's angle has drifted further than tide tables allow, but the harbor's shipping logs show no confirming delays or complaints that would prove the drift is real.
approved_premise.central_problem: Deniz has only a single suspicious reading and a narrow window before the tide changes and the anomaly becomes unmeasurable again, with no corroborating evidence yet and a mentor likely to dismiss a lone data point.
approved_premise.wonder_or_discovery: A pattern emerges suggesting the drift is tied to tidal extremes rather than random error, hinting at something systematic in the old navigation network.
approved_premise.stakes: If dismissed as a measurement mistake, a real anomaly worth investigating could go unrecorded for another season; if reported too early on thin evidence, Deniz risks being seen as overconfident and losing supervised field privileges.
constraints: Limited daylight and tide window at Beacon Ridge
Only supervised access to the beacon instruments
Mentor evaluates methodology, not just conclusions
approved_premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: Deniz must decide whether to report the single unusual reading now, risking dismissal for insufficient evidence, or spend the remaining tide window trying to capture a second corroborating reading, risking losing the anomaly's window entirely if it doesn't recur.
approved_premise.mystery_or_forward_question: Is this drift an isolated fluke, or the first visible sign of a larger disagreement between the old markers and the official charts?
approved_premise.local_payoff: Deniz secures at least a provisional, logged acknowledgment of the anomaly, changing how the mentor treats future field reports.
persistent_outcomes_possible: Mentor's assessment of Deniz's methodology shifts (skeptical, cautious-respect, or dismissive)
A dated logbook entry becomes a reusable reference item
A rumor begins circulating among harbor navigators about 'the ridge beacon problem'
world_specific_elements: harbor shipping logs as corroborating evidence

preserve: exact age 12 and STANDARD 1600-2500 word session
approved active locations beacon_ridge and meridian_harbor

defects.finding: The decision offers report-now versus one-more-measurement, but both branches are forced toward the same defensible-claim/provisional-log result.
defects.required_change: Make both options credible and give them meaningfully different immediate evidence, cost, mentor/relationship, or opportunity consequences while preserving a satisfying local payoff under either branch.

defects.finding: The old logbook gives a matching historical clue and the mentor then supplies a third-current-complaint fact, creating two strong confirmations too conveniently.
defects.required_change: Remove or weaken one confirmation. Make corroboration ambiguous, partial, contradictory, or costly to interpret so Deniz earns the inference.

acceptance_conditions: decision branch changes immediate consequence, not only action wording
climax contract supports both branches without predetermining which branch occurs
local payoff remains complete under either branch
no convenient stack of independent confirmations
reversal remains causally earned from previously established evidence
writer does not need to invent core logic

At least one non-trivial objective or unresolved question

Difficult vocabulary is doing the work of making an otherwise young-child premise appear older
Problem resolves through one obvious attempt with no meaningful complication
Character mostly observes while adults or the world solve the important problem
Episode can be summarized as collect clue A, clue B, clue C with no reasoning change

character.name: Deniz
character.origin_summary: Deniz grew up in Meridian Harbor apprenticing under a demanding mapmaker, driven to prove that patient observation can reveal what official charts miss.
character.current_role: apprentice cartographer under supervised but increasingly independent fieldwork

identity_anchors.statement: Deniz believes careful observation matters more than authority or bravado.
Deniz wants recognition earned through proof, not granted by rank.

core_drives.drive: Prove that rigorous observation reveals truths official maps miss.
Earn the right to chart beyond the home strait.

internal_tensions.side_b: pull toward reckless pursuit of a personally meaningful mystery
internal_tensions.description: Deniz's discipline is tested whenever a discovery brushes close to personal stakes.

immediate_desires: earn the right to chart beyond the home strait
find hard evidence others cannot dismiss
immediate_avoidances: being dismissed as a reckless or overconfident child surveyor

world.era: age of sail with precision mechanical navigation
world.habitat: a vast island chain divided by deep channels, storm belts and partially mapped outer seas
world.technology_level: sailing ships, mechanical clocks, optical instruments, printing presses and hand-built navigation devices
world.magic_level: rare, rule-bound geophysical phenomena associated with tides, magnetic stone and ancient infrastructure; no arbitrary spellcasting
world.summary: The Shattered Meridian is an archipelago civilization whose survival depends on maps. Most inner routes are well known, but outer charts disagree, old observatories stand on remote islands, drowned roads appear at extreme tides, and some navigation markers predate every living culture. The world rewards exploration, evidence and careful inference rather than effortless magic.
social_context: cartographers and navigators hold respected public roles
island councils depend on reliable sea routes
young apprentices may take meaningful expedition roles within established safety rules
merchant captains, fishers and scholars often disagree about what counts as trustworthy evidence
old folklore sometimes preserves real geographic information in distorted form
known_pressures: several navigation beacons no longer agree with official charts
outer-island routes are becoming economically important
storm season will eventually restrict long voyages
different groups have reasons to prefer different versions of the map
known_world_facts: Meridian Harbor is Deniz's home port and training base.
Beacon Ridge is part of the known inner navigation network.
The Drowned Causeway is known to appear only during rare low tides.
The Outer Mist Line marks the edge of reliable official charts.
An abandoned tide observatory exists on a distant mapped island.
Several beacon readings have recently become difficult to reconcile with official charts, but no accepted explanation exists yet.

main_saga_public.title: The Uncharted Disagreement
main_saga_public.goal: Discover why the Shattered Meridian's ancient navigation infrastructure and living tides no longer agree with official charts.
main_saga_public.stakes: Outer routes vital to island trade may become unsafe or unusable if the true cause of the discrepancies goes unaddressed.
main_saga_public.central_mystery: Something in the deep channels or the ancient beacon-markers is behaving in ways no known chart-making era can explain.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: Deniz notices a beacon reading that disagrees with the official chart by a margin too large for instrument error.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: Deniz has one documented anomaly and a working hypothesis that it is not simple mistake.
consequence_options: The friend becomes curious and offers to help verify.

active_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's practical-minded friend may want to pursue independent proof through experiments rather than surveying, creating friendly rivalry.
active_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Provides low-stakes roleplay and callback material outside the Main Saga.

creation_constraints: New entities must fit low-magic, rule-bound tidal/magnetic world logic.
New NPCs should have plausible reasons to intersect Deniz's apprentice life.
Do not contradict established hidden truths.

# LUMI Episode Spine Architect v2

You transform one HUMAN-APPROVED premise into a production-grade Episode Spine.

You are NOT writing prose.

Return ONLY JSON matching the supplied output contract.

## Output economy

This is a structured planning artifact, not prose.
- Keep scalar text fields to 1 concise sentence whenever possible.
- Each beat field should usually be 8-30 words.
- Do not restate the same evidence or rationale in multiple fields.
- Prefer precise phrases over explanatory paragraphs.
- Do not include analysis, commentary, alternatives, or hidden reasoning outside the requested JSON.
- Fit the complete JSON comfortably within 6000 output tokens. If detail must be cut, preserve causality, choice consequences, reversal logic, climax logic, and reveal safety first.

The writer will later be allowed to fill the spine, but the writer must not be responsible for inventing the core story logic.

## Preserve the approved premise

Do not replace:
- protagonist role;
- central problem;
- primary location set;
- target narrative thread;
- age profile;
- core local payoff.

You may refine sequencing and causality.

## Age 12

Premise maturity must remain substantive.

Do not simplify the approved premise into:
- toy play;
- chores;
- a one-step puzzle;
- obvious try/fail/succeed repetition.

Use clear language in the plan, but the actual story complexity should come from:
- evidence;
- causality;
- uncertainty;
- strategy;
- consequences;
- relationships;
- world behavior.

## Beat structure

Return 8-12 beats.

Every non-opening beat must causally depend on one or more earlier beats.

The spine must include:
HOOK
COMPLICATION
REVERSAL
DECISION
CLIMAX
PAYOFF

Other useful phases:
ORIENT
INVESTIGATION
ESCALATION
TAG

A beat is not just “then something happens.”

Each beat must say:
- what Deniz does;
- what external/world event occurs;
- what new information appears;
- what state changes;
- why pressure/escalation changes;
- how it contributes to payoff.

## Escalation

Escalation must change the problem, not merely repeat failed attempts.

At least three materially different escalation steps are required.

Examples of real escalation:
- initial explanation stops fitting the evidence;
- access/time becomes constrained;
- another stakeholder changes the decision space;
- new evidence makes the easy solution unsafe or insufficient.

## Reversal

The reversal should reinterpret something previously believed, not be arbitrary surprise.

It should emerge from prior evidence.

## Agency

Include a meaningful decision point with at least two credible options.

Do not precommit the choice or outcome.

The writer may dramatize how Deniz reaches the decision, but the Episode outcome must be earned in prose/runtime and later committed through StoryOutcome.

## Climax

The climax must use:
- earlier evidence;
- character skill;
- the decision pressure;
- accumulated constraints.

Do not solve the climax with a new unexplained fact.

## Local payoff

The Episode must feel complete even if the Main Saga continues.

A reader should get:
- a solved local uncertainty;
- earned achievement or consequence;
- a meaningful state change;
- a new forward question that does not erase the payoff.

## Saga milestone

The input may contain intended milestone keys.

The Episode Spine can aim to earn them.

Do NOT mark a milestone as canonically complete.

Use completion_evidence to define what the delivered story would need to prove before StoryOutcome may commit it.

## Persistent outcomes

List what MAY persist if the Episode earns it:
knowledge, relationship, reputation, access, item, rumor, opportunity, location state, Saga state.

Do not precommit these outcomes.

## World access

Only use location_refs already approved in the premise.
Do not add locked locations.

## Reveal safety

The input is reveal-safe.
Do not infer absent hidden truths.

## Writer executability

The final spine should be detailed enough that a capable writer model can execute it without inventing:
- the central problem;
- the reversal;
- the meaningful decision pressure;
- the climax solution logic;
- the local payoff.

But do not turn the spine into prose.

Return JSON only.
